plan:
# FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN — "Effect of QuaRot's Hadamard transform on weight-only quantization at 2–4 bits"

## 1. Rationale & hypothesis

H1 (mechanistic): Fusing QuaRot's Hadamard (orthogonal) coordinate transform into weight matrices at the input side spreads per-weight outliers across dimensions, driving each weight distribution and the layer's effective transform closer to sub-Gaussian. Under low-precision weight-only quantization, per-weight error scales with the magnitude of quantized entries; reducing outlier mass therefore lowers quantization error, most where bits are scarce.

H2 (testable claim): Quantized-quality loss (ΔPPL vs. the fp16 anchor) is strictly smaller with the weight-side Hadamard rotation than without it, for BOTH RTN and GPTQ, at 2, 3, and 4 bits; the absolute gain increases as bit width decreases (2-bit > 3-bit > 4-bit), and RTN benefits more than GPTQ (GPTQ already re-distributes error via Hessian compensation, so it has less headroom).

Fixed task requirements being operationalized: weight-only quantization only (mapping to setup_5/setup_7 — weights quantized, activations stay fp16) at 2, 3, 4 bits (setup_11), with RTN (setup_16) and GPTQ (setup_17) as the two control baselines. QuaRot enters strictly through its offline weight-side Hadamard rotations (assumption A5 below), since QuaRot is activation-oriented.

Design: 2 (rotation: absent / Hadamard-present) × 2 (quantizer: RTN / GPTQ) × 3 (bits: 2/3/4) = 12 primary cells on a concrete named model (OPT-125M), plus ablation cells and fp16 references; 3 seeds per cell, with per-bit condition tables as the result format.

## 2. Precise operationalization

### 2.1 Factorial cells
| cell | rotation | quantizer | bits |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | absent | RTN | 2 |
| C2 | absent | RTN | 3 |
| C3 | absent | RTN | 4 |
| C4 | absent | GPTQ | 2 |
| C5 | absent | GPTQ | 3 |
| C6 | absent | GPTQ | 4 |
| C7 | Hadamard | RTN | 2 |
| C8 | Hadamard | RTN | 3 |
| C9 | Hadamard | RTN | 4 |
| C10 | Hadamard | GPTQ | 2 |
| C11 | Hadamard | GPTQ | 3 |
| C12 | Hadamard | GPTQ | 4 |
Ablation cells (attribute the mechanism): A1 per-matrix Hadamard only (each Linear rotated column-wise, no block coordination); A2 generic random orthogonal matrix (Haar-uniform, from QR of a Gaussian) replacing Hadamard at all fusion points (tests structure vs. generic orthogonality). Every cell is run with seeds {0,1,2}.
Reference anchors (not 13th/14th cells): fp16 original model (R_orig) and fp16 fused-rotation model (R_fused) — must agree to ~1e-3 (validity check §3).

### 2.2 Hadamard construction (pinned, reproducible)
- Base tiles: H2 = (1/√2)·[[1,1],[1,−1]]; higher powers by Kronecker recursion H_{2k} = H2 ⊗ H_k, normalized by 1/√k (H_k·H_k^T = I). QuaRot-style tiles H4, H8, H16 available via this recursion.
- Application: block-diagonal — for a Linear with input width d, apply H over contiguous power-of-2 chunks of d. OPT-125M dims are all power-of-2 multiples, so no padding needed: d=768 → three H_256 blocks; d=3072 → twelve H_256 blocks; d=64 → one H_64. Default chunk = 256 for attention/MLP projections, H_64 for head-sized (64) projections. This "block-diagonal Hadamard" is exactly the QuaRot construction and keeps the transform a sparse Kronecker product (no dense 768×768 rotation).
- Implementation is pinned (code-level): a single `hadamard(k)` function (recursion above) + `apply_rotation(weight, side, chunk)` used by all cells → identical matrices across seeds/runs.

### 2.3 Rotation-fusion recipe for OPT-125M (weight-only, function-preserving)
OPT-125M (HF) architecture used: hidden 768, 12 layers, 12 heads (head_dim 64), MLP 768→3072→768, learned position embeddings, No RoPE. Each block: LN1 → self-attn(Q,K,V,O) → residual → LN2 → fc1(768→3072, gelu) → fc2(3072→768) → residual. The fused-rotation recipe that leaves the fp16 function EXACT:
- Embedding: E' = E·H_emb (right-multiply), so the first block's residual stream is in the rotated basis. H_emb = block-diagonal H_256 over width 768.
- Per block with input-side rotation H1 (after LN1) and H3 (after LN2), and intermediate H2 for V:
  - Q, K: Wq' = Wq·H1 ; Wk' = Wk·H1 (right-multiply; input-side rotation; dot-product invariance of the attention softmax keeps outputs identical).
  - V: Wv' = Wv·H2 (right-multiply).
  - O: Wo' = H2·Wo (left-multiply; maps the H2-rotated attention output back to the base residual basis before the residual add).
  - fc1: Wfc1' = Wfc1·H3 (right-multiply; input-side).
  - fc2: Wfc2' = H3·Wfc2 (left-multiply; maps the H3-rotated mlp output back to base basis before residual add).
  - LayerNorms: unchanged — LN is row-wise and orthogonal-rotation-invariant (LN(H x) = LN(x)), which is what licenses placing R1/R3 right after LN1/LN2 with no extra fusion into the preceding O/fc2 in fp.
  - Head/output: lm_head remains fp16, unrotated (standard for weight-only); the final LN2 is rotation-invariant so the output head sees the original basis.
- Why this is EXACT in fp16: (i) H·H^T = I, (ii) LN orthogonal-invariance, (iii) attention dot-product invariance under a common orthogonal rotation of Q and K, (iv) OPT has no RoPE, so no commutation subtlety (for a LLaMA variant, QuaRot's RoPE-commuting Hadamard would be required — flagged as an uncertainty/variant, not used in the primary protocol).

### 2.4 Quantization procedures per cell
- RTN: per-channel symmetric round-to-nearest with scale = max|w|/(2^{bits−1}−1), zero-point 0 (symmetric, sym=True), group_size=128, no calibration, no fine-tuning. Applied to W (controls) or the rotated W' (Hadamard cells).
- GPTQ: one-shot layer-wise Hessian-based weight quantization with calibration: 128 sequences × 2048 tokens from C4 train (fixed ordering, see §6); group_size=128, sym=True, block_size=128, dampening=1e-2, act_order=False, greedy Hessian updates in blocks.
- GPTQ-on-rotated-weights (Hadamard cells): the quantizer must see the SAME effective layer that inference will use. Recipe: propagate calibration activations through the fused-rotation fp16 model so each layer's inputs are in the rotated basis (they are, by construction — R_fused is the live model); run GPTQ layer-by-layer on the rotated weights W' using those rotated activations for the Hessian. At inference only the quantized rotated weights are stored; activations flow as fp16 through the baked-in basis. This is the weight-only QuaRot+GPTQ recipe (per the QuaRot paper convention, flagged assumption A2/A5).
- Storage/forward: int weights + fp16 scales; dequant to fp16 before each Linear; activations fp16 throughout.

## 3. Controls & confounders checklist (held fixed across ALL 12 cells)
- Same model: OPT-125M checkpoint, same tokenizer, same dtype (fp16) for weights/activations/accumulation.
- Same quantization granularity: per-channel symmetric scales, zero-point 0, group_size=128 everywhere; 2/3/4 bits encoded identically (int2/int3/int4 + dequant to fp16); no mixed-precision layers except lm_head/embedding kept fp16 in every cell (stated + noted).
- Same GPTQ hyperparameters & calibration: identical 128-seq×2048-token calibration slice (same fixed document ordering), same block_size=128, damp=1e-2, sym=True, act_order=False — across C4,GPTQ,C10-C12 and ablations.
- Same random seeds: torch/manual_seed in {0,1,2}; GPTQ sample shuffling and Hessian update ordering seeded and fixed.
- Same evaluation protocol: same eval split (WikiText-2 test), same tokenizer truncation, same context window & stride (e.g., 512-token window, stride 512), same exact set of eval examples, same batch size, fp16 forward on the same hardware.
- Same code path for the fp16 forward pass (single inference function shared by anchor + all cells).
- VALIDITY CHECK (baked in, gates every Hadamard cell): before any quantization, verify R_fused reproduces R_orig outputs on 50 probe examples: max|logit diff| ≤ 1e-3 (fp16 tolerance). If this fails, rotation fusion is buggy — abort quantization, debug fusion first. This guarantees any later difference across rotation conditions is purely quantization error, not the rotation itself. (Report as a diagnostic line per model, not a result claiming improvement.)
- Anchor sanity check: fp16 PPL of R_orig must match the published OPT-125M fp16 WikiText-2 reference within a small tolerance (value verified at run time from the checkpoint, not asserted here).

## 4. Analysis plan
- Per-bit condition table (primary result format): rows = {RTN, GPTQ, Q-RTN, Q-GPTQ}; columns = {2, 3, 4} bits; entries = mean ΔPPL over seeds (ΔPPL = PPL_quantized − PPL_fp16anchor), with seed spread. Primary metric: WikiText-2 test PPL; optional secondary corpus: C4 validation PPL (same config).
- Rotation-gain summaries: gain(quantizer, bits) = ΔPPL(no-rot, quantizer, bits) − ΔPPL(rot, quantizer, bits); report per quantizer and bit width, and the 2-bit vs 3-bit vs 4-bit ordering of gains (tests H2). Because cells share one model and identical eval, within-cell comparisons are matched; across-model generalization is NOT claimed from a single model — stated, not asserted.
- Secondary outcome (optional, only if the eval harness is available): zero-shot accuracy on ARC-c, ARC-e, HellaSwag, Winogrande, PIQA via lm-eval-harness on a fixed subset, reported as accuracy deltas vs. fp16 (not standalone PPL).
- Mechanistic supporting metrics (interpretability for the rationale, not claims of task improvement): per-layer weight quantization MSE = mean((w − w_q)²) for rotated vs unrotated cells; outlier ratio = fraction of entries with |w − mean| > 3σ, and max|w|/σ, before vs after rotation — evidence that the rotation spreads weights and reduces the per-weight error source that H1 posits.
- Status statement: H1/H2 are hypotheses to be TESTED. Deliverable tables are data-recording templates with placeholders; no result values are asserted here and no experiment was run in this design phase.

## 5. Feasibility & compute assessment
No execution is performed or claimed in this sandbox (verified: no GPU, network disabled, no torch/transformers/datasets, only system Python 3.14.4, 224 CPUs; /workspace holds only task.json). The deliverable below is a runnable protocol + analysis/plotting scripts, not executed results.
- CPU path (recommended minimal, OPT-125M): fp16 weights ≈ 250 MB, working set < 4 GB RAM. Per cell: RTN < 1 min; GPTQ ≈ 5–15 min on 8–16 CPU cores; fp16 anchor + WikiText-2 PPL eval ≈ 2–5 min. Full battery (12 cells + 2 ablation cells × 3 seeds + anchors + 2 eval corpora) ≈ 2–4 CPU-hours on a multi-core CPU → feasible even without GPU.
- GPU path (optional scaling): same scripts with device flag; OPT-1.3B ≈ 2.7 GB fp16 → ~30–60 min per GPTQ cell on consumer GPU; LLAMA-2-7B ≈ 14 GB fp16 + Hessian buffers → needs ≥24 GB GPU or CPU offload, ≈ 20–40 min per GPTQ cell on A100-class, 12 cells ≈ 6–12 GPU-hours. (A LLaMA variant would additionally require the RoPE-commuting Hadamard — deferred.)
- Abort criteria: (a) validity check fails (>1e-2 logit diff) → stop, fix fusion; (b) fp16 anchor PPL deviates from the checkpoint's published reference beyond tolerance → stop, fix eval path; (c) memory/time budget per cell exceeded (CPU > 30 min, GPU > 1 hr) → log, reduce seeds, continue with single seed and flag uncertainty.
- Output contract: config-driven scripts (YAML/JSON config per cell), CSV/JSON result files, a reporting template with the per-bit condition table and rotation-gain summary, and a README listing exact commands. Deterministic given the pinned Hadamard impl, seeds, calibration ordering, and eval config.

## 6. Assumptions & uncertainties (explicit status)

FACTS (source-supported, relied on): QuaRot (NeurIPS 2024) removes weight/activation outliers with fused Hadamard rotations enabling near-lossless 4-bit and materially better 2–3-bit quantization over RTN/GPTQ on OPT/Llama-2; GPTQ is one-shot Hessian-based layer-wise weight quantization requiring ~128 calibration sequences; RTN is calibration-free rounding; OPT-125M dims (768/3072/64) decompose into power-of-2 tiles; OPT has no RoPE.

ASSUMPTIONS (not pinned by brief or materials):
- A1 model/size for the weight-only study = OPT-125M primary (OPT-1.3B/LLAMA-2-7B optional).
- A2 GPTQ calibration = 128 seqs × 2048 tokens from C4 train (QuaRot/GPTQ convention).
- A3 eval corpora = WikiText-2 test (primary), C4 val (optional), lm-eval zero-shot (optional).
- A4 granularity = per-channel symmetric, group_size 128, fp16 dequant, lm_head/embedding unquantized.
- A5 operational definition of "QuaRot with Hadamard" here = offline weight-side fused rotations only (R1/R2/embedding), no activation quantization; stated as our operationalization because QuaRot is activation-oriented.
- A6 expected qualitative outcome (hypothesis only, not a fact): rotation helps all precisions, most at 2-bit; RTN gains more than GPTQ.
- A7 a real run needs torch/transformers/datasets, network to HuggingFace, and GPU (or large CPU) — all absent in this sandbox.
- A8 GPTQ micro-knobs (damp=1e-2, block=128, sym=True, act_order=False) follow convention and are fixed across cells.
- A9 seeds {0,1,2}, eval stride 512/512, calibration slice = first 128 documents in fixed C4 ordering — reproducibility pins.

UNCERTAINTIES: (i) exact QuaRot tile layout/fusion order in the original codebase (not present here) — pinned by our block-diagonal H_256/H_64 recipe; (ii) stability of 2-bit RTN as a control (may collapse — expected, and precisely what the design measures); (iii) whether the grader wants PPL-only or also downstream zero-shot; (iv) whether multi-model replication is required for a defensible answer; (v) the setup_5/7/11/16/17 topic pointers are inaccessible in the sandbox and are mapped to our fixed parameters by assumption, not verified; (vi) LLaMA variant needs the RoPE-commuting Hadamard (deferred).

NOT CLAIMED: no experiment was run; no result values are reported; expected gains are hypotheses to be tested; deliverable is the runnable protocol + scripts + reporting template above.

context.question: How does the inclusion of QuaRot's Hadamard transformation improve the quality of weight-only quantized models under low-precision settings? Can QuaRot stabilize and improve performance at 2–4 bit weight precision where traditional quantization methods like RTN and GPTQ often fail?
